title: Five Supports the Lord's Operative Power Has Set Within the Proprium's Body
reading:
Even within the natural mind as the proprium has organized it — within the very body that self-love has built for itself — the Lord's operative power has set five structural supports, running like veins and channels through what would otherwise collapse in on itself. These are five great works by which the Lord holds the natural mind in being, sustains it from beneath, and keeps it open to regeneration even in the midst of its claiming.

The first is the bearing-disc set upon the shoulder of what carries the whole from below: the celestial good that takes up the weight of the natural mind and holds it firm so that it does not fall into its own abyss.

The second is the path of regeneration itself, stretched forth through the very midst of the natural — the way upward planted not at the edge of the soul's claimed territory but driven straight through its center, so that ascent is always possible from wherever the soul stands.

The third is the Lord's shaping hand on the formation of the lowest states. Even the regions where self-love has its deepest hold are not left without form; the Lord molds and orders them, so that what is most fallen still bears a structure he has set.

The fourth is the four supporting pillars whose feet stand in the great mass of natural perception, at the ultimate degree of the natural mind. Down where the soul's perceptions are stirred and bitter, the Lord has driven foundations: the natural is not bottomless, it rests on what he has placed.

The fifth is the fourfold wall encircling the proprium's fortified strongholds — the bound the Lord sets around the soul's most fixed self-loving structures, so that even what the soul has hardened against him is enclosed within his order, and nothing of self-love finally escapes the limit he has drawn.

Thus the Lord's operative power runs through the very body of the proprium, holding it up, threading the way of return through its middle, shaping its lowest forms, planting foundations beneath its perceptions, and setting walls around its enclosures — preparing in advance, from within the soul's own claiming, the structure by which it will be regenerated.
